Run this setup chunk first (it rebuilds `nhanes_adults` exactly as in earlier
labs).

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(NHANES)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 14))

nhanes_adults <- NHANES |>
  filter(SurveyYr == "2011_12", Age >= 20) |>
  distinct(ID, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(
    id = ID, age = Age, gender = Gender, race = Race1,
    education = Education, income_mid = HHIncomeMid, poverty = Poverty,
    height = Height, weight = Weight, bmi = BMI,
    bp_sys = BPSysAve, bp_dia = BPDiaAve, pulse = Pulse,
    tot_chol = TotChol, sleep_hrs = SleepHrsNight,
    phys_active = PhysActive, smoker = Smoke100n,
    alcohol_days = AlcoholYear, diabetes = Diabetes,
    health_gen = HealthGen
  )

ed <- nhanes_adults |> drop_na(bp_sys, education, age)
```

# Part A: The education gradient (11:40-12:10)

## A1. Know your factor

Before modeling, inspect the factor.

```{r}
#| eval: false
levels(ed$education)
table(ed$___)
```

**Which level will `lm()` use as the reference, and how do you know?** ...

## A2. Unadjusted gradient

```{r}
#| eval: false
m_un <- lm(bp_sys ~ ___, data = ed)
summary(m_un)$coefficients |> round(3)
```

**Complete: "College graduates average ___ mmHg ___ (higher/lower) systolic BP
than the reference group, ___ (which group?), before any adjustment."** ...

## A3. Add age

```{r}
#| eval: false
m_adj <- lm(bp_sys ~ education + ___, data = ed)
summary(m_adj)$coefficients |> round(3)
```

**What happened to the education dummies when age entered, and why? (Think
Week 3: who is older in this sample?)** ...

## A4. One factor, one test

The four dummy t-tests do not answer "does education matter at all?" Run the
joint F test:

```{r}
#| eval: false
m_age_only <- lm(bp_sys ~ age, data = ed)
anova(___, ___)
```

**Report the test in one sentence: F statistic, degrees of freedom, p-value,
and the plain-language conclusion.** ...

## A5. Relevel and verify nothing changed

Make `College Grad` the reference and refit.

```{r}
#| eval: false
ed2 <- ed |> mutate(education = fct_relevel(education, "___"))
m_rel <- lm(bp_sys ~ education + age, data = ed2)
round(coef(m_rel), 3)
all.equal(fitted(m_adj), fitted(___))
```

**The printed coefficients changed but `all.equal()` says the fitted values
are identical. Reconcile those two facts in one sentence.** ...
